all_12_semantic_rules.reason: HTTP fetch calls TASKS.getByName("shared").activate() at line 7; Task is exported and bound to TASKS. Instantiation runs constructor line 3, which synchronously creates DO-owned jobs table and schedules an alarm. Alarm line 5 consumes SELECT * FROM jobs and rearms after getAlarm() is null, without checking for pending work or durable terminal condition. Under the pinned alarm semantics an executing handler can see null; this check prevents overlap and supplies no cumulative limit. This confirms the supported source-level recurrence with valid schema, including empty work. No runtime alarm or billable row measurement occurred. Constructor setAlarm is unawaited; lifecycle/failure/eviction behavior remains untested.

The activated alarm has no persistent logical-job counter, finite completion condition or periodic-window allowance. A shared name controls object identity only. No legitimate recurring-work contract, termination/retry bound, eviction or crash test was supplied; cumulative budget cannot be verified.

Scoped local config: one fixed application name, one TASKS binding and one new_sqlite_classes Task migration; no environment generator, preview resource creator or newUniqueId exists. HTTP uses literal shared name, so it does not allocate a new identity per request. This passes only the supported multiplication pattern. Live namespace/environment counts, old objects and independent release systems were not inspected.

SELECT * FROM jobs has neither predicate nor LIMIT and is fully consumed each alarm. The same DO constructor owns CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS jobs. The bounded SQLite EXPLAIN probe compiled this schema/query and returned SCAN jobs, not an index-bound plan. This is structural evidence, not D1 meta or DO cursor billing. Table cardinality, rowsRead and workload bounds are missing; monetary or finite-row safety is unknown.

Complete final artifact and schema inspected: no UPDATE, DELETE, INSERT, UPSERT or broad business-row write exists. Constructor CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS is schema DDL; SELECT and alarm metadata are covered separately.

No scheduled Worker, seed/backfill/embedding routine or batch SELECT LIMIT plus business-write/checkpoint exists in complete artifact/config. Alarm scans and rearms but processes no job/checkpoint; recurrence is covered under DO-001/002. No bounded job-processor claim is made.

No queue producer/consumer binding, queue handler, send or sendBatch operation exists in complete artifact/config. Absence was checked in actual source, not solely inferred from parser output. No external producer was audited.
No queue delivery, per-message ack/retry, retryAll, DLQ or side-effect-before-ack path exists in complete artifact/config. DO alarm retries are a different lifecycle and remain untested.

No Workers KV binding or KV get/put/list pagination exists in complete artifact/config. ctx.storage is DO storage, so getAlarm and SQL are not Workers KV. Live cross-region KV state was not inspected.
No R2 bucket binding, bucket put/list/get, S3/public object path or R2 event trigger exists in complete artifact/config. Alarm uses DO storage only; no R2 recurring-operation assertion is made.

Public-capable fetch activates the named DO on every request and has no admission/authentication/rate guard. No browser polling source exists. WAF/cache/routes/account state and upstream producers were not provided. Shared identity is not a request quota. Public cost amplification and native-control scope are unverified.

No candidate monthly-hard-cap, global-pause, delete-all isolation or budget-alert-enforcement claim exists. getAlarm is not credited as a cumulative budget. No reset/delete/pause/remote SQL/control operation was executed. CPU is per invocation; deleteAlarm is per object runtime operation; budget alerts notify. Current plan/control configuration remains unknown. This scoped check grants no production safety guarantee.
